title: Dining room area
summary: How many square meters of dining room you need for the number of covers you want.

what: To size the dining room you use an area per customer, which depends on the shape and size of the tables, how they're arranged and the category of the place, plus a percentage for walkways.
It tells you, before renting, how much space you need for the number of covers you want to serve.
formula: Area needed = area per customer × (1 + circulation %) × number of customers

variables.name: Area per customer
variables.description: Between 1.10 and 1.50 m² per person, depending on the tables and the category of the place.

variables.name: Circulation
variables.description: Between 10% and 20% extra so customers and staff can move comfortably.

variables.name: Covers
variables.description: How many customers you want to seat at the same time.

steps: Choose the area per customer that fits your concept.
Multiply by the number of covers.

examples.title: Tea house with 20 covers (handbook)
paragraphs: 1.10 m² per person + 20% circulation = 1.32 m² per person.
20 covers × 1.32 m² = 26.4 m², which the handbook rounds to 27 m².

notes.text: As a rule of thumb, the kitchen takes 15% to 25% of the premises, the dining room 45% to 65%, and storage and services 20% to 35%.
The handbook says that with 1.10 m² you need "between 1.20 and 1.30 m²" per person; the exact figures are 1.21 m² (10%) and 1.32 m² (20%).
If a space doesn't have the meters for your covers at the planned comfort level, the handbook recommends passing on it rather than giving up profitability or the concept.

area-per-customer.label: Area per customer
area-per-customer.placeholder: Square meters per person, between 1.10 and 1.50 (e.g. 1.10)
area-per-customer.hint: More space between tables = a more upscale place and more meters.

circulation-percentage.label: Circulation
circulation-percentage.placeholder: Extra percentage for walkways, between 10 and 20 (e.g. 20)

customers.label: Covers
customers.placeholder: Number of customers seated at the same time (e.g. 20)

steps.area-per-customer: Per customer with circulation = {areaPerCustomer} m² × (1 + {circulationPercentage}) = {areaPerCustomerWithCirculation} m²
steps.required-area: Area = per customer × covers = {areaPerCustomerWithCirculation} m² × {customers} = {requiredArea} m² (then rounded up)
